minutes.headline: Selectmen adopted town traffic rules, a five-year road-cut moratorium policy and IT policies; fee schedule deferred.
minutes.summary: The board heard public comment urging 24/7 police and fire coverage and worries about the future of town center buildings. It approved a one-day alcohol license, a Historical Society event and a toll booth location change, then adopted the traffic rules and regulations and an amended road-opening moratorium policy. It also adopted IT resource policies, heard committee and town manager reports, and went into executive session on litigation.

public_comment.topic: Asked the board to direct the town manager to convene officials and report on getting 24/7 police and fire coverage, without an override.
Apologized for an earlier angry comment and voiced concern about the future of Town Hall, Ritter and old primary buildings if offices move to TC Passios.
Concern that the road-cut moratorium could block development that adds tax revenue; offered Planning Board help with notice.

what_happened.line: The Select Board adopted the traffic rules and regulations, with corrections to the school zone section and handicapped parking near the Lane property.
The board approved a five-year road opening moratorium policy with amendments, including 14-day decisions and a fee set by the fee schedule.
The board adopted information technology resources policies for employees, boards and commissions.
The board approved a one-day beer and wine license, a Historical Society lot use and a toll booth fundraiser location change.
A resident asked the board to direct the town manager to report on 24/7 police and fire coverage without an override.

why_it_matters: The road opening policy limits when streets can be cut, and the fee for a permit is not yet set, so costs to builders and utility customers are still open.
The traffic rules set parking and traffic fines and need state approval before they take full effect, so enforcement may not change right away.
Foreclosed property sales will add revenue that affects free cash, which feeds into future budget and tax decisions.
watch_next: The Sept 19 agenda, where the water district is to be asked to come on its permit and withdrawals.
A road-opening fee schedule from the DPW director, and the state approval timeline for the traffic rules.
